source.rights: Historical American Type Founders specimen published in the United States in 1898; public domain by age.
source.role: Whole observed dollar and independent six-point optical/scale comparisons.

accepted_physical_scale.method: One isotropic least-squares scale from independently selected common capitals; no target g/dollar, R alternatives or M variants in fit.

accepted_row.method: Whole flat-footed r/b/m/l/n/h shapes anchor Theil-Sen baseline; targets and rounded forms excluded.

selected.decision: The LOC six-point dollar before 2468, at threshold 155, retains both native apertures and the printed bar and terminal extents. Twelve independent capitals and ten flat-footed text anchors support scale and row alignment. The filled collective dollar and threshold 110 with a broken lower contour are rejected. Modern 35-unit sidebearings are used; no punctuation is invented.

recipe.notes: The LOC six-point dollar before 2468, at threshold 155, retains both native apertures and the printed bar and terminal extents. Twelve independent capitals and ten flat-footed text anchors support scale and row alignment. The filled collective dollar and threshold 110 with a broken lower contour are rejected. Modern 35-unit sidebearings are used; no punctuation is invented. Four-times Lanczos sampling preserves the native evidence; no hole filling or independent stretching is applied.

loc6-text.method: Whole flat-footed r/b/m/l/n/h shapes anchor Theil-Sen baseline; targets and rounded forms excluded.

reviewed: Native page, point-labelled setting, selected whole-form crops and independent capital comparisons visually reviewed.
Measured text baseline checked against native letter feet; selected mask, threshold range and preliminary word settings reviewed.
identity_limit: Matching same-size optical design supported by common capitals and lowercase; no punch, matrix or first-casting identity claimed.
quality_todo: Seek a sharper six-point m shoulder; the current census impression is retained.
Seek further clear same-size punctuation; filled collective impressions do not justify drawing missing strokes.
rejected: The collective six-point m and the six- and eight-point dollars are heavily filled and remain comparison evidence.
The Ryan g in Vaulting has a broken upper bowl at threshold 175; lower thresholds lose more contour detail.
The LOC dollar at threshold 110 loses its lower closure.
